document.title: Lanternworks booking review
summary: Booking a studio mostly works, but two people can still end up with the same room. Fix that before the spring courses open; the other three findings are smaller and can be decided on their own.
This is an invented review of an invented product. It shows what a decision document holds and how each part reads.

startWith.reason: Two members were both told the same studio was theirs. It is the one finding that costs trust on the day.

order.label: First
order.title: Make a confirmed booking mean one room for one person
order.summary: Close the double-booking gap before anything else is built on top of the calendar.
order.why: Every other finding assumes that a confirmation can be trusted.

order.label: Then
order.title: Decide how members hear about full classes and failed payments
order.summary: Both change what a member is told when something does not go through.
order.why: They touch the same notification settings, so deciding them together avoids doing that work twice.

order.label: Any time
order.title: Settle the cancellation window
order.summary: A policy question more than a product one.

sources.label: BOOKING_REVIEW.md
sources.detail: the invented review this example is built from

sources.label: Three synthetic captures and one diagram
sources.detail: drawn for this example; no real product is shown

sections.title: What the review covered
bullets: Booking a studio and a class as a member, on a phone and on a desktop browser.
The staff calendar for one studio across one week.

sections.title: What it does not establish
bullets: How often double bookings happen in production; the review reproduced one and did not measure a rate.
Anything about payments beyond the one failed renewal described in BOOK-003.

items.title: Two members can be confirmed for the same studio and time
items.status: Open in the review · reproduced twice on 14 January
items.summary: Two members who pressed Book within two seconds of each other were both confirmed for Studio B from 10:00 to 12:00. Each saw the normal confirmation screen, and the staff calendar showed both bookings side by side.
items.impact: One of them arrives to a room that is taken, and staff find out at the door. A confirmation that cannot be relied on undermines every other part of booking.
steps: Two members open the same free slot on their own phones.
Both press Book within about two seconds.
Both get a confirmation; the calendar holds two bookings for one room.

evidence.label: Staff calendar
evidence.caption: The staff calendar after the test: two confirmed glazing sessions in Studio B from 10:00 to 12:00, made two seconds apart.

evidence.label: Second member's phone
evidence.caption: The second member's confirmation. Nothing on it says the slot had just been taken.

evidence.label: What the two attempts recorded
evidence.caption: Read from the booking log after the second reproduction.
rows: 2 for the same studio and time
none, to either member or to staff

evidence.label: How it happens
evidence.caption: Both requests read the slot as free before either booking is saved, so both are saved.
evidence.source: Drawn from the sequence and times in BOOKING_REVIEW.md, section 2.1 (synthetic)

options.name: Hold the slot the moment Book is pressed
options.summary: The first request takes the slot; the second is told it has just gone and is shown the nearest free times.
benefits: A confirmation always means the room is yours.
The member who loses the race finds out at once, while they can still pick another time.
tradeoffs: Needs a change where bookings are saved, and a new message for the member who was second.

options.name: Keep booking as it is and alert staff to conflicts
options.summary: Both bookings still go through. Staff get a notice and sort it out by phone.
benefits: Small change, with nothing new for members to learn.
tradeoffs: A member is still told a room is theirs when it is not.
Relies on staff seeing the notice in time, including at weekends.

noChange.label: Leave booking as it is
noChange.description: Accept that double bookings happen and are handled at the door.

recommendation.summary: Hold the slot when Book is pressed, and tell the second member straight away.
reasoning: The problem is that the app says something untrue to a member. Only the first option stops that; the staff alert leaves the untrue confirmation in place and adds work for staff.
It is also the option that keeps working as bookings grow, because it does not depend on anyone noticing.

items.uncertainty: The review reproduced the double booking twice but did not measure how often it happens. If it is rare, the staff alert may be enough for a first release.
items.evidenceLimits: Tested with two phones on the staging site. The class-booking flow, which has places instead of rooms, was not tested for the same gap.
successCriteria: Repeating the two-phone test leaves one booking, and the second member sees that the slot was taken.
The staff calendar never shows two bookings for one room and time.

items.title: A full class offers no way to wait for a place
items.summary: When a course is full, the page says so and stops. A member cannot join a waiting list, ask to be told when a place opens, or see the next start date.
items.impact: Interested members leave with nothing to do, and places that open after a cancellation stay empty unless someone happens to look again.

evidence.caption: The page for a full six-week course: a disabled button and a line asking the member to check back later.

evidence.label: Places that opened and stayed empty, by course
evidence.caption: Ten places opened on full courses in the last four courses. None was taken, because nobody was told.

options.name: Add "Tell me when a place opens"
options.summary: One button. Everyone who pressed it gets a message when a place frees up, and the first to book gets it.
benefits: Simple to explain and to build.
tradeoffs: First come, first served can feel unfair to whoever asked first.

options.name: Add an ordered waiting list
options.summary: Members join a queue. When a place opens it is offered to the next person for a set time.
benefits: Staff can see real demand for a course.
tradeoffs: More to build: the queue, the offer, the time limit, and what happens when an offer lapses.
Members have to act on an offer in time or lose it.

options.name: Link to the next start date
options.summary: Keep the page as it is and add the next date for the same course.
tradeoffs: Does nothing for places that open on the full course.

recommendation.summary: Start with "Tell me when a place opens", and add the next start date beside it.
recommendation.reasoning: It answers the member's question with the least to build, and how many people press the button shows whether a full waiting list would be worth its cost.

items.uncertainty: Nobody has asked members which they would prefer. The fairness concern is a guess.
items.successCriteria: A member on a full course can leave with something to expect, and a place that opens is taken within a day.

source.title: Full classes are a dead end

items.title: A failed renewal cancels the membership without telling the member
items.status: Open in the review · seen once
items.summary: When a monthly renewal failed, the membership was set to `cancelled` the same night. The member got no message and first learned of it when a booking was refused.
items.impact: A member with an expired card loses access and their standing bookings in one step, with no chance to fix the card first.

evidence.label: Renewal log for the test account
evidence.caption: The only three lines the renewal job wrote. There is no retry and no message between the failure and the cancellation.
evidence.text:
02:00:04  renewal  member=test-417  charge failed: card_expired
02:00:04  renewal  member=test-417  status active -> cancelled
02:00:05  renewal  member=test-417  released 3 future bookings

options.name: Give a seven-day grace period with reminders
options.summary: Keep the membership active for seven days, message the member on days 1, 4, and 7, and cancel only after that.
benefits: Most failed cards are fixed without anyone losing a booking.
tradeoffs: A member who never pays keeps access, and their held slots, for a week.

options.name: Cancel as now, but tell the member first
options.summary: Send one message when the charge fails and cancel the next night.
benefits: Smallest change that ends the silence.
tradeoffs: One day is short notice, and standing bookings are still released.

recommendation.summary: No option is recommended until the studio says how long it is willing to hold slots for an unpaid membership.
recommendation.reasoning: Both options end the silent cancellation. Which is better depends on how scarce studio time is, and that is a business call the review has no evidence for.

items.evidenceLimits: Seen on one test account with an expired card. Other failure reasons, such as insufficient funds, were not tried.

items.title: The 24-hour cancellation window is stricter than members expect
items.summary: Members can cancel a studio booking for free up to 24 hours before it starts. Two of five people in the review tried to cancel later than that and were surprised to be charged.
items.impact: The rule works as designed. The question is whether it is the rule the studio wants.

options.name: Shorten the window to 12 hours
options.summary: Free cancellation up to 12 hours before the booking.
benefits: Matches what the people in the review expected.
tradeoffs: Less time to rebook a freed studio, so more of them may stand empty.

noChange.label: Keep the 24-hour window
noChange.description: Leave the rule as it is and make it easier to see when booking.

recommendation.summary: Keep the 24-hour window, and show it on the booking screen.
recommendation.reasoning: Five people is too few to change a policy on. The surprise came from not seeing the rule, and showing it costs far less than empty studios would.

items.uncertainty: Based on five people. A larger group could point the other way.
